findings.text: blocking: the sentence 'the three tests pass at their exact tolerances (logs/fix-three-tests.log, 5 passed)' rests on a log that carries no revision header, no command line and no EXIT= line, and no completed full-file gate exists at the fix revision: logs/fix-equilibrium_test_topology_read.py.log writes '# revision: e3de3c290...' (the pre-fix head) and its mtime is 17:30 against a fix committed at 17:22, so the fragment's claim is unattributable to 0ff6d2318 and done_when (3) is unmet for tests/equilibrium/test_topology_read.py, the file that imports the module this increment changes. The sibling citation at :244, logs/fix-device-and-identity.log, likewise carries no revision and no EXIT= line.

non-blocking: the diagnostic figures 'membership fraction of 0.011', '264 node rows' and '8.3e-32 in the eager path against 7.1e-3 in the compiled one' appear in no file under the run's logs/ directory; grep for 0.011 and 8.3e-32 over logs/ returns nothing, and the four probe logs the manifest cites for round4_diagnosis (probe-geom-base.log, probe-geom-head.log, probe-dups-head.log, probe-geom-fix.log) report only duplicate-vertex counts and cell coordinates. The values exist only in the worker transcript resume-4.jsonl, so the fragment presents measurements no later reader can open.

non-blocking: 'The cells carry six corners each' is contradicted by the run's own probe: logs/probe-geom-head.log reports 'CELLS 132 VCOUNT [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10]' and lists cells 48 to 53 carrying eight slots each (slots 1,2 and 6,7), so the polygons reaching the atomiser hold three to ten vertices, not six.

non-blocking: this call is written to a file outside the brief's declared write scope (nova/equilibrium/stencil_mesh.py, nova/equilibrium/analytic_single_null.py, nova/biot/plasmagrid.py, their test files, tests/test_carrier_vertex_identity.py and the fragment); the worker names the breach in the manifest's round4_fix key rather than stopping for a scope grant, so the coordinator must ratify the addition of topology.py to the node's scope.

non-blocking: round4_gate states 'tests/equilibrium/test_topology_read.py at 0ff6d2318 is running as job 1294861', but the job's log header, written by its own script with git -C <worktree> rev-parse HEAD at launch, records '# revision: e3de3c290cd707986419863f62dfa54c81b34cfe'; a reader cannot tell from the record which revision the gate measured, and the job was still RUNNING 25 minutes in against a 59-minute limit.

verdicts.diff: Read both commits against e3de3c290: 0ff6d2318 factors _representative_polygons behind a public canonical_polygons wrapper in nova/equilibrium/stencil_mesh.py:455 and calls it from nova/equilibrium/topology.py:2529; 42563384c adds one 38-line fragment section, and no test file is changed in either commit.
verdicts.done_when: done_when (3) requires every test file importing the changed modules to pass by delta in its own fresh process; the increment adds nova/equilibrium/topology.py to the changed set, and tests/equilibrium/test_topology_read.py imports TopologyGeometry at :469 and :507, but its gate log logs/fix-equilibrium_test_topology_read.py.log is uncollected and its header records revision e3de3c290, so no completed arm exists at the fix.
verdicts.goal: The node goal is to make the hex carrier device-independent and the analytic reference solve deterministic; this increment addresses the follow-on regression those changes caused in the topology read, and nova/equilibrium/topology.py:2529 now feeds canonical polygons to the atomiser.
verdicts.manifest: Read the run manifest (status complete); it declares twelve commits and records the topology gate as running and uncollected at its checkpoint line, but its round4_gate line states the job runs at 0ff6d2318 while the job's own log header names e3de3c290.
verdicts.write_paths: Read the run manifest's orientation_write_paths and the brief's write-only list; nova/equilibrium/topology.py, touched at 0ff6d2318:2527-2529, is in neither, and the worker records the breach itself in the round4_fix key.
